sentences.text: The allegations leveled by the complainant above were against one lawyer namely Gauri Shankar Bairwa and his office associates.

In her complaint she alleged serious allegations of rape, making obscene video of her,
wrongful confinement, extortion of money etc. by the alleged at his office in Madangir, New Delhi.
As per the contents of the complaint prima facie a case was registered in the relevant sections of law and investigation taken up by her.

During investigation, all the SOP laid own was followed and victim had corroborated her version before the doctor during her medical examination as well as in the statement U/s 164 Cr.P.C before the Hon'ble Magistrate in Saket Court.

During investigation,
notice was issued to the alleged accused Gauri Shankar Bairwa to join the investigation.
He did not turn up and filed for Anticipatory Bail.
On 23/10/2021, he granted the anticipatory bail from the court of Sh. Anil Kumar, Ld. ASJ, Saket.
After that, again notices were sent to him.
On 10/11/21, at around 3:06 PM, he came to police station along with his advocate associates and she was busy in Saket Court.
At 3:07 PM he called her on her mobile phone but due to court decorum her phone was on silent mode and due to that she could not attend his phone.

When Ct Case No.

4. Arguments on the application were advanced by the complainant.
5. The allegations revealed in the complaint in paragraph 23 can be segregated into two parts.
In the first part, it is alleged that the respondent was demanding sum of Rs 7 Lacs for closing the false case against the complainant.

This part of the allegation is the subject matter Ct Case No. 217/2020 Gauri Shankar Bairwa Vs W/SI Mukesh Page No. 11 of 13 of Prevention of Corruption Act and this Court is not an appropriate forum to take cognizance of this part of the complaint against the respondent as there are designated Courts dealing with complaints under the Prevention of Corruption Act and complainant is at liberty to approach the appropriate forum.

sentences.text: 6. In so far as second part of the allegation is concerned, complainant stated that when he refused to pay the said amount, respondent deliberately used the 'jati suchak' words against him which are already noted above.

The position in regard to prosecution under Section 3(1)(r)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred to as 'SC & ST Act') is already settled that the casteist remarks ought to be hurled in public view.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 7. To fortify this, I draw the support of Judgment of Allahabad High Court in Pintu Singh @ Rana Pratap Singh & Ors Vs State of U.P. date of decision 10.05.2024 wherein the Court reiterated that the alleged act of intentional insult or intimidation causing humiliation would constitute an offence only if it is committed in public view.

entities.text: Pintu Singh @ Rana Pratap Singh & Ors Vs State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Analyzing the present complaint in light of the afore-noted position, the complaint is devoid of the details as to when, where and in front of whom the alleged castiest remarks were made by WSI Mukesh.
Even if it is assumed that the alleged incident took place in a police station, there is no averment that it happened under public view.

The Ct Case No. 217/2020 Gauri Shankar Bairwa Vs W/SI Mukesh Page No. 12 of 13 plain averment that the respondent used 'jati suchak' remarks against the complainant is not sufficient to move the wheels of criminal justice by issuing direction under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. in the absence of essential requirement of Section 3(1)(r)(s) of the SC &
ST Act being not complied with.
